question: A haulage engineer is reporting the total force, in newtons, on a twin-cart train: 1 N for a coupling spring, plus 2 times the force for a single cart, where each cart's force includes 2 N of bearing drag on top of the force needed to accelerate its 189 kg mass. The carts are 2.5 m long. The acceleration, in m/s², equals the area under the curve y = 4x² + 5x from x = 3 to x = 4. What is the total force, in N?

A club treasurer is reporting the net energy balance, in kilojoules, for 3 identical launch runs. Each run's balance is the projectile's energy of motion, expressed in kilojoules, minus 19 kJ drawn from the launcher's battery. The projectile has a mass of 10 kg. Its speed, in m/s, is found by multiplying the sum of 5 and 6 by 3 and then subtracting 23. What is the net energy balance, in kJ?

A rail operator is compiling the total energy of motion, in kilojoules, of 9 trains, each with 7 identical wagons, with each train's total expressed in kilojoules. Each wagon's contribution is its energy of motion less 13 J lost to coupling slack. Each model wagon has a mass of 46 000 g. Each wagon's speed, in m/s, equals the number of ways to choose 2 wagons from 12. What is the total energy of motion, in kJ?

A physics club is reporting the combined energy of motion, in joules, of 6 groups of 2 identical carts. Each cart has a mass of 53 000 g. Each cart's speed, in m/s, is found by taking the area under the curve y = 2x² + 5x from x = 2 to x = 3 and subtracting 21. What is the combined energy of motion, in J?

A wind-turbine technician needs the net energy balance, in kilojoules, of a test nacelle's battery: 14 kJ is added by a charger at the end, and before that 23 kJ is drawn by the yaw motor. The starting figure is the energy of motion of the 45 kg test blade tip, expressed in kilojoules. The tip speed, in m/s, equals the rate at which the slope of the curve y = 4x³ + 1·x² is itself changing at x = 1. What is the net energy balance, in kJ?

A haulage firm wants the total force, in kilonewtons, across 11 depots, each with 3 bays, each with 7 identical trucks pulling at once. Each truck pulls an 89 000 g test sled. The sled's acceleration, in m/s², equals the area under the curve y = 3x² + 4x from x = 3 to x = 4. What is the total force, in kN?

A 49 000 g cart is accelerated at a rate, in m/s², equal to the larger root of x² - 9x + 20 = 0. The depot runs 11 carts per line and 9 lines at once. The combined force is expressed in kilonewtons, and 8 kN of it is supplied by a shared gravity chute, which the motors need not provide. What force, in kN, must the motors provide?

A safety officer is reporting a final figure, in kilojoules, for a set of 6 test lanes: it is 6 times the net figure for one lane. The net figure for one lane is the combined energy of motion of 6 identical carts, expressed in kilojoules, minus 9 kJ absorbed by the lane's buffer. Each cart has a mass of 28 kg and each lane is 20 m long. Each cart's speed, in m/s, equals the area under the curve y = 2x² + 6x from x = 0 to x = 2. What is the final figure, in kJ?

A dock foreman wants the net force, in kilonewtons, that a winch supplies: the force for 6 identical pallets accelerating at once, less 23 N supplied by a slope. Each pallet has a mass of 25 kg and is 1.2 m wide. The acceleration, in m/s², is the smaller root of x² - 10x + 24 = 0. What is the net force, in kN?

An 8 kg test puck is launched across an air table at a speed, in m/s, equal to the sum of the whole numbers from 1 to 11. The lab launches 2 identical pucks at once, and the pair's energy of motion is expressed in kilojoules. The experiment is repeated 2 times. What is the total energy of motion, in kJ, over the 2 repeats?

A 20 kg trolley is pushed along a hospital corridor at a speed, in m/s, equal to the sum of the squares of the whole numbers from 1 to 5. Along the way, a push adds 23 J to its energy of motion, a ramp adds 29 J, a second push adds 21 J, and a final nudge adds 7 J. What is the trolley's energy of motion, in J, at the end?

A shipyard wants the total force, in kilonewtons, on 9 identical winch lines, each pulling 2 model hulls at once. Each hull has a mass of 176 000 g. The hulls' acceleration, in m/s², equals the slope of the curve y = 5x³ + 1·x² at x = 1. What is the total force, in kN?

A speedway engineer is compiling the total energy of motion, in kilojoules, for 2 heats of 5 races, each race with 2 identical bikes, with each race's figure expressed in kilojoules. Each model bike has a mass of 22 000 g. Each bike's speed, in m/s, is 2 times the sum of 2 and 15. What is the total energy of motion, in kJ?

A cargo airline wants the total energy of motion, in joules, of every container it moves in a day: 8 hubs, each with 10 belts, each moving 8 identical containers. Each model container has a mass of 22 kg. Each container's speed on the belt, in m/s, equals the area under the curve y = 2x² + 6x from x = 0 to x = 2. What is the total energy of motion, in J?

A fleet manager is reporting the total force, in newtons, for 12 identical trucks, less 27 N recovered by a shared regenerative rail. Each truck's figure is the force to accelerate 6 identical 25 000 g crates at once, less 17 N supplied by a tailgate spring. The crates' acceleration, in m/s², is 2 times the sum of 7 and 20. What is the total force, in N?

A port authority wants the total force, in kilonewtons, on 7 identical cranes, each stated in kilonewtons. Each crane's force is what it takes to accelerate 5 identical 186 000 g containers at once, plus 14 N for cable drag. Each container is 6 m long. The acceleration, in m/s², equals the area under the curve y = 1·x² + 7x from x = 3 to x = 4. What is the total force, in kN?

A physics teacher wants the final energy figure, in kilojoules, for a demonstration: 16 kJ from a heater, plus 4 kJ from a spring, plus the combined energy of motion of 3 identical carts, expressed in kilojoules. Each cart has a mass of 48 kg and the track is 5 m long. Each cart's speed, in m/s, is the greatest common divisor of 70 and 114. What is the final figure, in kJ?

A depot wants the total force, in kilonewtons, on 3 identical model wagons accelerating at once. Each model wagon has a mass of 156 000 g. The acceleration, in m/s², is 12 times the smaller root of x² - 11x + 24 = 0. What is the total force, in kN?

A fleet engineer wants the net force, in newtons, on a trolley after a final 21 N push, before which 14 N of drag was subtracted, and before that 11 N of tailwind was added to the force needed to accelerate the trolley. The trolley has a mass of 66 000 g and is 1.4 m long. Its acceleration, in m/s², is the smaller root of x² - 10x + 24 = 0. What is the net force, in N?

A harbour engineer is computing the net forward force, in kilonewtons, on a model tug after an 11 kN backward hawser pull is applied. Before that, the forward force is the force needed to accelerate the 125 kg model, plus 8 N from a fan and 13 N from a current, expressed in kilonewtons. The acceleration, in m/s², is the larger root of x² - 13x + 40 = 0. What is the net forward force, in kN, with backward forces counted as negative?

A 50 000 g crate is accelerated on a conveyor at a rate, in m/s², equal to 9 times the smaller root of x² - 7x + 6 = 0. The conveyor is 15 m long. The plant runs 8 crates per line and 2 lines at once, and a shared drive adds 26 N of belt friction to the total. What is the total force, in N?

A physics teacher wants a final figure, in kilojoules: 2 kJ from a spring, plus the energy of motion of a 42 kg cart expressed in kilojoules. The cart's speed, in m/s, is obtained from a gauge reading by subtracting 30 and then adding 29. The track is 4 m long. The gauge reading is the larger root of x² - 7x + 10 = 0. What is the final figure, in kJ?

A depot wants the force, in kilonewtons, to accelerate a 172 000 g wagon. The wagon is 3 m long. Its acceleration, in m/s², is 9 times a base value, and the base value is the smaller root of x² - 11x + 30 = 0, plus 2, minus 1. What is the force, in kN?

A depot wants the total force, in kilonewtons, for 3 lines, each with 3 identical 112 kg carts accelerating at once. The acceleration, in m/s², equals the rate at which the slope of the curve y = 4x³ - 5x² is itself changing at x = 1. The carts all share one drive. What is the total force, in kN?

A lab wants the total energy of motion, in joules, of 6 groups of 3 pairs of identical 16 000 g carts. The track is 2 m long. Each cart's speed, in m/s, equals the area under the curve y = 5x² + 2x from x = 0 to x = 1. What is the total energy of motion, in J?
